label: Elements of Differential Geometry
notes: This chapter spans printed pages 109 through 130 and assembles the geometric machinery information geometry rests on. The guiding question is what extra structure lets local tangent planes knit together into curved geometry, and the answer threads through metrics, connections, geodesics, and curvature.

label: Manifolds and Tangent Spaces
notes: A tangent space is the local linear arena at a point, the first-order model of a curved surface there. A tangent vector appears as an arrow, a directional derivative operator, or, on a statistical model, a score random variable. These are three faces of one geometric object.

label: The Riemannian Metric
notes: A Riemannian metric supplies an inner product on each tangent space, written in coordinates as a positive definite matrix. Lengths and angles of tangent vectors become measurable. On probability models the Fisher information matrix is the natural metric, since it is the inner product of score functions.

label: Metric as a Local Ruler
notes: On the unit sphere the line element is one in the latitude direction but scales with sine squared of the colatitude in longitude. The same unit displacement therefore leaves a different coordinate footprint at different latitudes, which the metric ellipse field makes visible as stretched measuring devices.

label: Affine Connections
notes: A metric compares vectors inside one tangent space, but an affine connection compares vectors across neighboring tangent spaces. Its Christoffel coefficients record how the coordinate basis itself rotates and stretches from point to point, and the covariant derivative corrects ordinary component derivatives by that basis motion.

label: Christoffel Symbols on the Sphere
notes: For the round sphere the symbolic computation gives the longitude-longitude Christoffel symbol of the colatitude as minus sine times cosine, and the mixed symbol as cotangent of the colatitude. These coefficients are exactly what the covariant derivative subtracts to keep differentiation coordinate independent.

label: Geodesics and Parallel Transport
notes: A geodesic keeps its own tangent direction parallel to itself, the connection's notion of a straightest path. Parallel transport carries a vector along a curve with vanishing covariant derivative. The geodesic generally departs from the naive straight chart line, which is only a coordinate artifact.

label: Curvature and Holonomy
notes: Riemann-Christoffel curvature is the infinitesimal failure of parallel transport around a closed loop to return a vector unchanged. Equivalently it is the obstruction to commuting two covariant derivatives. On the sphere the transported vector returns rotated, and that holonomy angle measures the enclosed curvature.

label: Fisher Geometry of Normals
notes: For the normal family in mean and log-scale coordinates the Fisher metric is diagonal with entries exp of minus twice the log-scale and two. Mean motion costs more when the distribution is narrow, while log-scale motion has constant Fisher cost. A Monte Carlo score estimate confirms the analytic matrix.

label: Submanifolds and Embedding Curvature
notes: A submanifold inherits tangent vectors and a metric by differentiating its embedding map. The induced connection is the ambient covariant derivative projected back, and the normal component is embedding curvature. A cylinder bends in ambient space yet carries zero intrinsic Riemann-Christoffel curvature, separating the two notions.

label: Takeaways
notes: Tangent spaces are local linear models, metrics measure tangent vectors with Fisher information as the statistical case, connections compare neighboring tangent spaces and define covariant derivatives, geodesics and parallel transport follow from the connection, and curvature records path-dependent transport distinct from extrinsic embedding curvature.
